sections.title: Taking part in a clothing exchange

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: The clothes exchange takes place once a term. I can register you now and explain how to drop items off before the public session.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: All right. Let’s go through the details.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: And what is the registration surname?

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: I have the surname Benson on the registration. Tell me if the letters on the confirmation are wrong.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Could you confirm the drop-off morning?

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: The drop-off is on Saturday morning. Friday is reserved for setting out tables and checking the room.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: What have you put down for the drop-off code?

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: Write M42 on your bag. The letter M is followed by four and two. This keeps it linked to your form.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: What should I write for the bag material?

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: Use a paper bag if possible. The volunteers can write on it and sort it without opening it.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: And what is the maximum items per donor?

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: Bring up to five items. If you have more, save the rest for the next exchange.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Could you confirm the items for the separate rack?

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: The separate rack is for coats. Shirts and trousers go on tables according to their size.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: What have you put down for the venue floor?

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: The exchange is on the ground floor. Do not follow the signs upstairs to the meeting rooms.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: What should I write for the time doors open?

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: The public doors open at 10:45, which is a quarter to eleven. Donors can arrive earlier to leave their bags.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: And what is the donation token colour?

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: The token will be purple. A green token was used last term, so check that you have the new one.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Could you confirm the contact point inside?

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: Ask at the desk just inside the door if you need help. The people at the clothes racks may be busy sorting.

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: I have your place on the list. You can bring a friend, but please ask them to register if they want to donate items.

script.speaker: Gardener
script.text: Please use the plan at the entrance to the rooftop garden. The cross shows our central junction, with north at the top. Paths are narrow because the planters need space around them.

script.speaker: Gardener
script.text: The seed cabinet is north of the junction, by the top railing. Its doors are labelled by plant type.

script.speaker: Gardener
script.text: The compost box stands east of the junction. Follow the right-hand path past the two short planters.

script.speaker: Gardener
script.text: The shade bench is south of the junction, under the fabric roof shown at the bottom of the plan.

script.speaker: Gardener
script.text: The water station is west of the central junction, beside the left railing where the pipe comes up from below.

script.speaker: Gardener
script.text: Use small cans on the roof. The large cans are heavy when full and can damage the narrow pots.

script.speaker: Gardener
script.text: Write each plant label with a pencil. Ink from the pens we used earlier became difficult to read.

script.speaker: Gardener
script.text: Leave empty pots in the crate beside the stairs. We count them before taking them down to the store.

script.speaker: Gardener
script.text: We will begin the main demonstration after the break. In the first session, just look at the layout.

script.speaker: Gardener
script.text: A volunteer will offer each visitor a small packet of seeds on the way out.

script.speaker: Gardener
script.text: Leave the middle passage clear for the trolley. It is used to carry the heaviest planters to the lift.

script.speaker: Gardener
script.text: Before leaving, check that you have taken any gloves or notebooks with you. We will close the roof as soon as the group returns downstairs.

sections.title: Planning a study of group work

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: Our education project looks at how students share turns during a group exercise. Let’s agree on what we will observe so the two groups get comparable instructions.

script.speaker: Jamie
script.text: All right. Let’s go through the details.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: We will count speaking turns. Counting words would take too long, and a mark for the loudest voice would answer a different question.

script.speaker: Jamie
script.text: Both groups will order picture cards. A written quiz would make them work alone, and the model-building task has more steps.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: The observer should sit apart from the group. Joining the discussion could change who speaks, and standing by one learner might make that person uncomfortable.

script.speaker: Jamie
script.text: Noor will make the picture cards. Jamie is arranging the rooms and Ellis will review the coding sheet.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: Jamie will reserve the rooms. If they are not available at the same time, we can move the observation to a different day.

script.speaker: Jamie
script.text: Ellis will review the coding sheet before the first session. We have asked for comments on instructions that could be interpreted in two ways.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: Start the timer when the cards reach the table, not when the students enter the room.

script.speaker: Jamie
script.text: Use a letter for each participant. This keeps the observer notes short and separates them from names.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: Add a separate column for uncertain cases. It is better to review them later than to guess during the exercise.

script.speaker: Jamie
script.text: Keep the completed sheets in the blue folder. The green one is for unused copies.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: If the trial is clear, we can use the same coding sheet in both sessions. We should agree how to handle doubtful cases before looking at the totals.

sections.title: Understanding the dry edge of a pond

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: A pond’s edge changes over a season. Today I’ll show how a short survey can describe the changes without confusing a falling water level with a movement of the bank.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Choose a post that will not move as the water rises and falls. Mark the starting point for your measurements on it.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Measure the distance to the water’s edge from the fixed point. Do not use the wet mark left from an earlier water level.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: A sketch can show where the ground is steep or flat. Include a few notes about places where the line crosses vegetation.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Take the photographs from the same position each time. A new viewpoint can make a small change look much larger.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Put a scale beside the patch of bare soil. Without it, the photograph will be harder to compare with the next one.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: A strip of leaves may have collected where water recently reached. It does not always show the current level.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Some banks collapse after water has removed material from the base. The top can look unchanged until the lower support has gone.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Write down whether there has been heavy rain recently. The note gives context for a level that seems unusually high.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Sample both the near and far shore if the route allows it. Water and wind can affect the two sides differently.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Put each observation in a dated log. This will help you match the written measurements with the photographs.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: A sequence of comparable visits can tell us more than one detailed visit. Keep the position and timing of each observation with the result.
